title: From sensor A to sensor B
summary: Sequence a move with a set and a reset: run the belt from sensor A until the box reaches sensor B.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Use a set and a reset to hold an output between two events.
Explain why a sensor that goes dark cannot hold the output by itself.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/LatchTwoSensors.st, make Run a latch: set it when EyeA sees the box and reset it when EyeB sees the box.
stages.checkpoint: Run stays on between the two sensors, and the reset wins over the set.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, follow the box: sensor A sees it for a moment, then the box moves on and A goes dark.
stages.checkpoint: Run turns on when A sees the box, stays on while the box travels, and turns off when B sees it and stays off.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then run: The starter never runs the belt; set Run when EyeA sees the box and reset it when EyeB sees the box.
stages.checkpoint: Check reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press Run (F5) and open the 3D view.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named latch-two-sensors and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare the moment A goes dark with the moment B turns on: the belt keeps running in between because Run holds its value.
stages.checkpoint: Both sensors count the box, Run is off at the end, and no box is dropped.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The assertions check the count at both sensors and the final state; they say nothing about how long the move takes in real life.
stages.checkpoint: What the assertions check is tested; nothing else is.

hints.text: The output itself can be the memory: an IF that writes TRUE to Run when EyeA is TRUE keeps the value on later scans.
Add a second IF after it that writes FALSE when EyeB is TRUE, so the reset wins when both sensors are TRUE.

faultCases: The starter never runs the belt; set Run when EyeA sees the box and reset it when EyeB sees the box.
